title: Social Security, reimagined: Cato's Romina Boccia brings the retirement debate to TAMIU Wednesday
excerpt: Romina Boccia of the Cato Institute speaks on 'Reimagining Social Security' at TAMIU on Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 6 p.m. — free and open to the public, with a livestream.
content:
What is Social Security, really — a savings account, a promise, or something else entirely? That question takes center stage at Texas A&M International University on Wednesday, November 11, when Romina Boccia, director of budget and entitlement policy at the Cato Institute, delivers the lecture "Reimagining Social Security: Political Narratives and Economic Reality," according to TAMIU.

The talk is set for 6 p.m. in the TAMIU Student Center Ballroom (STC 203), with doors opening at 5:30 p.m. It is free and open to the public, and it will also be broadcast live via Microsoft Teams at go.tamiu.edu/boccia. The event is part of the university's IBC Bank & Commerce Bank 2026-27 Keynote Speaker Series.

According to TAMIU, the lecture will examine Social Security's design, including the disconnect between the program's pay-as-you-go financing, the nature of the trust fund, and the widespread belief that workers are saving for their own retirement. Drawing on nationally representative polling conducted by the Cato Institute, Boccia will look at how Americans understand Social Security, where public perceptions diverge from reality, and how different ways of framing the issue affect support for reform.

Boccia focuses on federal spending, the budget process, the economic consequences of rising debt, and reforms to Social Security and Medicare. She is the principal author of the Substack newsletter Debt Dispatch and co-author of the book "Reimagining Social Security: Global Lessons for Retirement Policy Changes." She previously served as director of the Grover M. Hermann Center for the Federal Budget at the Heritage Foundation and was managing director at Dialog, an invite-only leadership network. A native of Augsburg, Germany, she holds bachelor's and master's degrees in economics from George Mason University.

For more information, contact TAMIU's Center for the Study of Western Hemispheric Trade at 956-326-2820 or cswht@tamiu.edu.
